$comment: KS-4910 / ADR-162 §4. Personal study lesson templates for StudyLessonBuilder. {{name}} placeholders are filled by the builder. Per-shelf overrides live in shelves.<key>; a missing shelf key falls back to common. Content enrichment is KS-4913; do NOT change the schema without backend approval.

noteLines.results: Your recent games: {{wins}} wins, {{losses}} losses, {{draws}} draws.
noteLines.carryOver: Carried over from the previous session: “{{theme}}” — see it through this time.
noteLines.noGames: No games yet — link chess.com/lichess or upload a PGN, and your lessons will be built from your own games.

common.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}” — according to your stats this is your main growth area right now. Don't guess: find the idea first, then make the move.
common.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself, in writing or out loud:

1. Where did the position first turn worse — and with which move?
2. Which move would you play differently now, and why?
3. Was there a tactical moment on “{{themeLabel}}” — for you or your opponent?
common.homeworkNote: Homework follows the lesson — it reinforces the topic until the next session. Unfinished homework carries over into the next lesson, so it pays to close it right away.

novice.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}”. Before every move, check all checks and captures — at your level almost every solution starts with one.
novice.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself:

1. Were there moves that left one of your pieces hanging without protection?
2. Did you see all checks and captures — yours and your opponent's — during the game?
3. Where could you have won material using the “{{themeLabel}}” idea?

beginner.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}”. The algorithm: find all forcing continuations (checks, captures, threats) first, and only then choose between them.
beginner.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself:

1. Where did the position first turn worse — a blunder or gradual drift?
2. Did you check your opponent's checks, captures and threats before every move?
3. Was there a tactical moment on “{{themeLabel}}”? Find it on the board.

intermediate.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}”. Before moving, name the motif to yourself: why does the combination work here — which piece is overloaded, which square is weak?
intermediate.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself:

1. Find three critical moments of the game and suggest two candidate moves in each.
2. Where did you play without a plan — a move that neither improved your position nor hindered your opponent?
3. Did your plan follow from the pawn structure of the opening, and was there a chance for “{{themeLabel}}” tactics?

advanced.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}”. Calculate lines to the end — to an evaluation of the final position, not to “looks good”. Check your opponent's in-between moves.
advanced.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself:

1. Mark the critical moments — where the game could have taken a different course. Do they match the places where you thought longest?
2. Where would prophylaxis have worked — asking “what does my opponent want?” before your own plan?
3. Evaluate the exchanges and transitions to the endgame: which were in your favour and which were not? Was a “{{themeLabel}}” tactic missed?

club_strong.puzzleInstruction: Solve puzzles on “{{themeLabel}}” in tournament mode: full calculation to an evaluation, checking candidate moves for your opponent, no moves “by eye”. Note where your calculation stopped short.
club_strong.gameSelfCheck:
Replay the game move by move (opening: {{opening}}) and answer for yourself:

1. Reconstruct your calculation in the key positions: where was the tree of variations incomplete — a candidate move for your opponent missed?
2. What type were your errors in this game: evaluation, calculation, psychology, opening preparation?
3. Compare your plans with the demands of the position: where should you have changed the character of the struggle, and was the “{{themeLabel}}” theme underestimated?
